newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium wants money supply targeting for ECB.
newsitem.headline: Belgium wants money supply targeting for ECB.

text.p: The future European Central Bank (ECB) should set money supply targets rather than inflation targets to implement its price stability policy, Belgian central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse said.

"The preference (among EU member states) seems to go towards a money supply policy. We too are in favour of this," he said at the presentation of the central bank's annual report on Wednesday. His comments were embargoed for release on Friday.

"Since a money supply policy gives more weight to developments in the monetary sphere, it connects more closely with the specific responsabilities of a central bank. It also makes it more easy to judge a central bank on the results of its policy," Verplaetse said.
Under current Belgian central bank policy the franc tracks the German mark closely, so the bank shadows the monetary policy of the Bundesbank, which uses money supply targeting.
A minority of European countries including Britain, however, use inflation targeting.
Final decisions on ECB policy will be taken once the ECB is set up in 1998. It will take over responsibility for monetary policy once the European single currency is launched in 1999.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
